title: Published inventory does not reconcile with Hotspawn's own fixtures API
detail: Hotspawn's API listed 97 CS2 fixtures when read at 2026-10-16T11:21:13Z; the deployed snapshot published 101 rows generated at 2026-10-16T08:18:38Z. Missing from the site: none. Published but no longer listed by Hotspawn: ['1079630', '1080286', '1080287', '1081493'], of which 3 had already passed their scheduled start when the API was read (1081493, 1080286, 1079630). Hotspawn's fixtures feed is queried with status=scheduled, so a fixture leaves it once it starts; that part is a timing difference between two readings, not a coverage gap. Still unexplained: ['1080287'] - published as upcoming although Hotspawn no longer lists them and their scheduled start had not passed. They may have been postponed or removed; this audit does not assume which. This difference is NOT explained by elapsed time and needs review. No row was added or removed by this audit.

title: A published pick cites a URL outside the official allow-list
detail: The deployed origination payload cites https://liquipedia.net/counterstrike/CCT/2026/Europe/Contenders_4 on fixture 1081529 (Nexus v WROTBERRY) at aliases_used[0].evidence[2].url. Those hosts are not in the OFFICIAL allow-list published in scripts/audit_rows.py, so the join they support is evidenced by a source the project's own policy does not accept. The offending URLs are quoted here rather than linked, because a flag's own source_urls must be official or the review row that renders them would fail the same policy.

title: An independent official line disagrees with the published pick for 1080287
detail: Voca vs HAVU (Elisa BreakOut Series #2, 2026-10-16T12:00:00Z): the site picks Voca from Polymarket via its market rung ([57.5, 42.5]%, observed 2026-10-16T08:18:27Z), while Polymarket (None, overround None, observed 2026-10-16T11:15:04.985645Z) de-vigs to HAVU ([32.8, 67.2]%). The two official sources are 24.66 percentage points apart, which is enough to flip the pick on a near-even match. Both are linked; neither was overridden, and no third opinion was invented to break the tie.

title: Picks are published on margins smaller than the spread of their own source
detail: The origination ladder publishes a pick for every fixture it can price and has no minimum-edge threshold (the deployed snapshot reports no_edge=0). 3 resolved fixture(s) are decided by less than 5 percentage points: 1079588 Astralis vs MIBR [48.5, 51.5]%; 1079588 Astralis vs MIBR [48.5, 51.5]%; 1079588 Astralis vs MIBR [48.5, 51.5]%. These are arithmetically correct and every one replays from its cited source, but a reader on a phone cannot distinguish a 1.5-point margin from a strong favourite. Reported as a presentation irregularity, not a data error.

title: Published probability for 1079630 has drifted more than 5 points from Polymarket's own archived prices
detail: ex-RUSTEC vs Saint Sinners (None, None): Polymarket event 1190750 (cs2-rustec-ssins-2026-10-16) quotes ['ex-RUSTEC', 'Saint Sinners'] at [0.815, 0.185] observed 2026-10-16T11:17:08.77416Z, while the site published [0.685, 0.315] observed 2026-10-16T08:18:26Z — a deviation of [13.0, -13.0] percentage points across a 2.98 h gap between the two readings. Both observations are kept; the gap between the readings is stated so drift is not mistaken for a defect. Neither was overwritten by this audit.

title: Published pick for 1080287 is now the underdog on the same source that produced it
detail: Voca vs HAVU (None, None): Polymarket event 1173319 (cs2-voc-havu-2026-10-16) quotes ['Voca', 'HAVU'] at [0.305, 0.695] observed 2026-10-16T11:15:04.985645Z, while the site published [0.575, 0.425] observed 2026-10-16T08:18:27Z — a deviation of [-27.0, 27.0] percentage points across a 2.94 h gap between the two readings. The favourite has flipped, so the published pick is the underdog on the current price from the very source that produced it. This is a freshness problem, not an arithmetic one: the published number still replays exactly from the quote it cites. Both observations are kept and neither was overwritten.

title: source_outcomes is published in market order while probabilities is in team order
detail: scripts/domain.py::market_analysis aligns `quotes` and `probabilities` to the fixture's team order but records `source_outcomes` in the market's own order. 2 published row(s) therefore carry the two arrays in opposite orders (1081497, 1080289). Every one was verified correct against Polymarket's own archived prices, so no published probability is wrong; but a reviewer comparing the two arrays positionally would invert the favourite. Nothing is rendered from `source_outcomes` on any page today.
